requirements.text: In case of non-replaceable LED modules, the ESA that is (part of) a light source shall be covered by a Technical Service test report stating that it is not mechanically interchangeable with any light source according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128; otherwise R10 approval of the ESA shall not be granted.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the LED module and connector interfaces against the R37/R99/R128 light-source cap and holder geometries, and obtain the Technical Service non-interchangeability report.

requirements.text: In case of a replaceable LED light source, the ESA that is (part of) a light source shall hold an approval according to Regulation No. 37, No. 99 or No. 128, and its approval number shall be specified; otherwise R10 approval of the ESA shall not be granted.
requirements.test_case: Check that a valid R128 (or R37/R99) approval number exists for the light source and appears in the application documentation.

requirements.text: An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA (rear combination lamp with LED modules on PCB) conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Inspect production samples to confirm that the R10 approval mark is present on each lamp.

requirements.text: The international approval mark on the ESA shall be affixed in the place specified on the approval communication form.
requirements.test_case: Compare the location of the mark on the lamp with the location stated in the approval communication form.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise a circle containing the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country granting the approval.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for a circle enclosing 'E' and the correct country number.

requirements.text: The approval mark shall comprise the number of this Regulation (10), followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, placed to the right of the circle.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the mark for '10R-' followed by the approval number to the right of the E-circle, and check it against the approval certificate.

requirements.text: The approval marking on the ESA, conforming to paragraph 5.3, need not be visible when the ESA is installed in the vehicle; it may be placed, for example, on the rear or inner side of the housing.

The ESA (rear combination lamp with LED modules and drive electronics) shall be designed, constructed and fitted so that the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, can comply with the requirements of UN R10.
requirements.test_case: Review the EMC design and confirm that all the R10 ESA tests below have been passed.

requirements.text: The ESA shall be tested for radiated and conducted emissions and for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
requirements.test_case: Check that the test plan and report cover radiated emission, conducted transient emission, radiated immunity and conducted transient immunity.

requirements.text: When measured by the method of Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically with frequency above 30 MHz), 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically with frequency above 75 MHz), and a constant 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Measure broadband radiated emissions per Annex 7 (CISPR 25 ALSE) from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare with the Appendix 6 limit line.

requirements.text: On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all measured broadband emission points lie below the limit line.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver (containing an electronic oscillator above 9 kHz, e.g. switch-mode/PWM or microcontroller), when measured by the method of Annex 8, the narrowband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed 52 to 42 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz band (decreasing logarithmically above 30 MHz), 42 to 53 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band (increasing logarithmically above 75 MHz), and a constant 53 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Measure narrowband radiated emissions per Annex 8 with an average detector from 30 to 1,000 MHz and compare with the Appendix 7 limit line.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver, the measured narrowband value on the ESA representative of its type, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify that all measured narrowband emission points lie below the limit line.

requirements.text: In case of a passive LED drive (the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz), the ESA shall be deemed to comply with the narrowband limits of paragraph 6.6.2 and Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Review the circuit schematic and BOM to confirm that no oscillator or switching device operates above 9 kHz.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on its 12/24 V supply lines, tested according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10, shall not exceed the maximum allowed pulse amplitudes given in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure conducted transient emissions on the supply line per ISO 7637-2 and record the positive and negative pulse amplitudes.

requirements.text: Maximum allowed transient pulse amplitude: in case of 12 V systems, +75 V positive and -100 V negative; in case of 24 V systems, +150 V positive and -450 V negative.
requirements.test_case: Compare the measured peak pulse amplitudes with the limits for the rated supply voltage.

requirements.text: If the ESA is not switched, contains no switches and does not include an inductive load, it need not be tested for transient conducted emission and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
requirements.test_case: Review the schematic for switches, switched operation and inductive loads (e.g. buck-converter inductors).

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to electromagnetic radiation shall be tested by method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9 (absorber chamber/ALSE, TEM cell, BCI, stripline or reverberation chamber).
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated immunity testing per Annex 9 with the chosen method(s).

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand radiated immunity test severity, applied by the Annex 9 methods, at the levels of Table 2a over more than 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz band and at not less than the minimum levels of Table 2b over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz band.
requirements.test_case: Apply the field or current levels per Annex 9 across the frequency range and log the achieved levels against the tables.

requirements.text: Test level over more than 90 per cent of the band: stripline 20 to 400 MHz 60 V/m; TEM cell 20 to 200 MHz 75 V/m; BCI 20 to 400 MHz 60 mA; ALSE 80 to 2,000 MHz 30 V/m and 2,000 to 6,000 MHz 10 V/m; reverberation chamber LUF to 2,000 MHz 21 V/m and 2,000 to 6,000 MHz 7 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the applied test level meets the Table 2a value over at least 90 % of the frequency points.

requirements.text: Minimum test level over the whole band: stripline 20 to 400 MHz 50 V/m; TEM cell 20 to 200 MHz 62.5 V/m; BCI 20 to 400 MHz 50 mA; ALSE 80 to 2,000 MHz 25 V/m and 2,000 to 6,000 MHz 8 V/m; reverberation chamber LUF to 2,000 MHz 18 V/m and 2,000 to 6,000 MHz 6 V/m.
requirements.test_case: Verify that no frequency point has an applied level below the Table 2b minimum.

requirements.text: During the radiated immunity tests performed in accordance with Annex 9, there shall be no degradation of performance of the immunity-related functions (stop lamp and rear position lamp function) of the ESA.
requirements.test_case: Monitor the stop and rear position lamp light output (e.g. photodiode/camera) during exposure and check for no unintended switching off, switching on or intensity change.

requirements.text: The immunity of the ESA to transient disturbances conducted along its 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, and shall achieve the functional status classifications of Tables 3a and 3b.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 7637-2 pulses and the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp supply and classify lamp behaviour per ISO 7637-1/ISO 16750-1.

requirements.text: Starting profile: immunity test level II for both 12 V and 24 V systems, 10 pulses; functions related to immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) shall achieve functional status B if the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, or C otherwise; functions not related to immunity-related functions (e.g. reversing lamp) shall achieve status D.
requirements.test_case: Apply 10 starting-profile pulses at level II and assess each lamp function's status per ISO 16750-1.

requirements.text: Pulse 1: -75 V (12 V) / -450 V (24 V), 500 pulses, FPSC III for all functions. Pulse 2a: +37 V / +37 V, 500 pulses, FPSC I for immunity-related functions, III for others. Pulse 2b: +10 V / +20 V, 10 pulses, FPSC II for immunity-related functions, III for others. Pulse 3a: -112 V / -150 V, 1 h, FPSC I for immunity-related functions, III for others. Pulse 3b: +75 V / +150 V, 1 h, FPSC I for immunity-related functions, III for others.
requirements.test_case: Apply each ISO 7637-2 pulse at the level for the rated voltage and verify the stop and rear position lamp functions meet FPSC I/II/III as tabulated.

requirements.text: The starting profile immunity requirement applies only if the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines started with a 12 V/24 V starter motor.
requirements.test_case: Check the intended vehicle applications and include the starting profile test where applicable.

requirements.text: Rear lamp ESAs approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6 (paragraph 7 not applicable, as the lamp is not used in REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid).
requirements.test_case: Run the paragraph 6 ESA tests (emission, radiated immunity, conducted transients) on production samples and compare the results with the type-approval results.

requirements.text: For a rear lamp ESA taken from series production, the measured broadband electromagnetic disturbance levels shall not exceed the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.5.2.1 by more than 4 dB (60 per cent).
requirements.test_case: Measure the radiated broadband emissions of a production sample per Annex 7 and check that they stay within the 6.5.2.1 limit plus 4 dB.

requirements.text: A rear lamp ESA taken from series production shall not exhibit any degradation relating to the direct control of the vehicle that could be observed by the driver or other road users (e.g. stop lamp or rear position lamp switching off or behaving abnormally) when subjected to a field strength, expressed in V/m, up to 80 per cent of the reference limits prescribed in paragraph 6.8.2.1.
requirements.test_case: Expose a production sample to radiated immunity testing per Annex 9 at 80 % of the 6.8.2.1 levels and monitor the lamp functions for any degradation.

requirements.text: A rear lamp component/STU taken from series production shall show no degradation of performance of its immunity-related functions (stop lamp, rear position lamp) up to the conducted transient immunity levels given in paragraph 6.9.1 for its 12 V or 24 V supply system.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 7637-2 test pulses of paragraph 6.9.1 to the supply lines of a production sample and verify that the required function performance status is met.

requirements.text: A rear lamp component/STU taken from series production shall not exceed the conducted transient emission levels given in paragraph 6.7.1 on its 12 V or 24 V supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Measure the conducted transient emissions of a production sample per ISO 7637-2 (Annex 10) and check the pulse amplitudes against the 6.7.1 limits.

requirements.text: In case the ESA is not exempted under paragraph 6.10 (e.g. an active electronic LED driver with switch-mode/PWM or microcontroller), the broadband electromagnetic interference radiated by the ESA (rear lamp), measured per Annex 7 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the ESA broadband reference limits: E = 62 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m for 30-75 MHz; E = 52 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m for 75-400 MHz; E = 63 dBµV/m for 400-1,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated broadband emissions of the lamp per Annex 7 (ALSE, 120 kHz bandwidth, 30-1,000 MHz) and compare against the Appendix 6 limit curve.

requirements.text: In case the ESA is not exempted under paragraph 6.10 (e.g. an LED driver containing a microcontroller, oscillator or other narrowband source), the narrowband electromagnetic interference radiated by the ESA (rear lamp), measured per Annex 8 with a 120 kHz bandwidth, shall not exceed the ESA narrowband reference limits: E = 52 - 25.13 log(F/30) dBµV/m for 30-75 MHz; E = 42 + 15.13 log(F/75) dBµV/m for 75-400 MHz; E = 53 dBµV/m for 400-1,000 MHz.
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated narrowband emissions of the lamp per Annex 8 (120 kHz bandwidth, 30-1,000 MHz) and compare against the Appendix 7 limit curve.

requirements.text: During the broadband emission test the rear lamp ESA under test shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load (e.g. rear position, stop and reversing lamp functions all energised).
requirements.test_case: Check the test report that the lamp was operated in normal mode with all LED functions on at maximum load during the CISPR 25 ALSE scan.

requirements.text: For an ESA not involved in 'REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid', the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated broadband emission measurement of the lamp per CISPR 25 clause 6.4 ALSE method and confirm the setup in the report.

requirements.text: The broadband emission limits of paragraph 6.5 shall be met throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an ALSE or OATS.
requirements.test_case: Scan radiated emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz and verify all readings are below the para 6.5 broadband limit line.

requirements.text: The broadband limits of paragraph 6.5 are quasi-peak limits; if peak detectors are used for the measurement of the rear lamp ESA, a correction factor of 20 dB as defined in CISPR 12 shall be applied.
requirements.test_case: Review the emission plot to confirm quasi-peak readings, or peak readings with the 20 dB correction, were compared with the para 6.5 limits.

requirements.text: In case of an active electronic LED driver (or where the exceptions of paragraph 6.10 do not apply), the lamp ESA shall be in normal operation mode, preferably at maximum load, during the narrowband emission test.
requirements.test_case: Check the test plan and setup record that all lamp functions (position, stop, reversing) are energised in normal operation at maximum load during the measurement.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission limits of paragraph 6.6.2.1 shall be met by the lamp ESA throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz, measured in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).
requirements.test_case: Measure radiated narrowband emissions from 30 to 1,000 MHz per CISPR 25 ALSE method and compare against the paragraph 6.6.2.1 limit lines.

requirements.text: The narrowband emission levels of the lamp ESA shall be evaluated with an average detector when compared with the limits.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test report that the narrowband scan used an average detector and that all readings are below the limit.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall comply with the immunity requirements using any combination of the following test methods, at the manufacturer's discretion, provided the full frequency range of paragraph 3.1 of Annex 9 is covered: absorber chamber (ISO 11452-2), TEM cell (ISO 11452-3), bulk current injection (ISO 11452-4), stripline (ISO 11452-5) or reverberation chamber (ISO 11452-11).
requirements.test_case: Review the immunity test plan and reports to confirm the selected ISO 11452 methods together cover 20 to 6,000 MHz.

requirements.text: The radiated immunity test conditions for the rear lamp ESA (frequency range and general conditions) shall be according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Check that the immunity test report states ISO 11452-1 general conditions were applied.

requirements.text: During immunity testing, the rear lamp ESA shall be switched on and stimulated to be in normal operation condition, with the stop lamp and rear position lamp functions active.
requirements.test_case: Verify in the test set-up and report that the lamp was powered and its stop and position functions were operating during exposure.

requirements.text: The rear lamp ESA shall be exposed to the immunity test signal over the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency step size and dwell time according to ISO 11452-1.
requirements.test_case: Perform the immunity sweep from 20 to 6,000 MHz with ISO 11452-1 steps and dwell times and check that the functions are not degraded.

requirements.text: In the 20 to 400 MHz range, the immunity test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be amplitude modulated (AM) at 1 kHz with 80 per cent modulation depth.
requirements.test_case: Apply 1 kHz, 80 % AM between 20 and 400 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: In the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz range, the immunity test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be pulse modulation type 2 (PM2): Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs.
requirements.test_case: Apply PM2 (3 µs on, 3,333 µs period) between 2,700 and 3,100 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: In the 380 to 2,700 MHz and 3,100 to 6,000 MHz ranges, the immunity test signal applied to the rear lamp ESA shall be pulse modulation type 3 (PM3): Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs.
requirements.test_case: Apply PM3 (500 µs on, 1,000 µs period) in 380–2,700 MHz and 3,100–6,000 MHz and monitor the lamp functions.

requirements.text: In case the absorber chamber method is used, the rear lamp ESA shall be exposed with vertical polarization, with the field conditions established by the substitution method according to ISO 11452-2.
requirements.test_case: Check that the absorber chamber report shows vertical polarization and substitution-method field calibration per ISO 11452-2.

requirements.text: In case bulk current injection is used, the rear lamp ESA shall be tested according to ISO 11452-4, either by the substitution method with the injection probe at 150 mm from the ESA or by the closed-loop method with the probe at 900 mm.
requirements.test_case: Check that the BCI report states the method used and the matching probe distance (150 mm substitution or 900 mm closed loop).

requirements.text: The ESA (rear lamp LED modules and drive circuitry) shall be immune to conducted transients on the vehicle power supply.
requirements.test_case: Perform the Annex 10 conducted transient immunity tests and check that the stop and rear position lamp functions keep their specified behaviour.

requirements.text: The ESA shall limit the conducted transients it generates on the vehicle power supply.
requirements.test_case: Measure the transient emissions on the supply lines per ISO 7637-2 and compare them with the applicable limits.

requirements.text: The ESA shall withstand test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to ISO 7637-2, applied to its 12/24 V supply lines and to other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines (e.g. stop, tail and reverse feed inputs).
requirements.test_case: Apply ISO 7637-2 pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b to every supply and switched-feed pin, and verify the lamp's functional status during and after each pulse.

requirements.text: Unless the ESA is exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles without a 12 V/24 V starter motor, the ESA shall withstand the starting profile according to ISO 16750-2, applied to its supply lines and to other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines.
requirements.test_case: Apply the ISO 16750-2 starting profile to the lamp's supply and switched-feed inputs, and verify that the lamp's functions stay within the specified behaviour.

requirements.text: The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on its 12/24 V supply lines, and on other connections that may be operationally connected to supply lines, shall be measured according to ISO 7637-2 and shall meet the applicable limits.
requirements.test_case: Measure the conducted transient emissions per ISO 7637-2 on each supply and switched-feed line while switching the lamp functions on and off, and compare the results with the limits.

requirements.text: Every lamp belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp drawing and sample to confirm a marking area large enough for all required markings.

requirements.text: All markings on the lamp shall be clearly legible and indelible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the markings for legibility and rub them with a solvent-soaked cloth to check they are indelible.

requirements.text: The value of dimension "a" of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure dimension "a" of the moulded or printed approval mark.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark, i.e. a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled E and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number that forms part of the approval number.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the 4- to 6-digit sequential number matching the approval.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Check visually that the sequential number sits next to the circled E mark.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbols identifying the light signalling lamp functions for which approval has been granted, as prescribed in paragraph 3.2.4.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the function symbols of all approved functions.

requirements.text: The function symbols in the approval marking shall be: R1 (rear position lamp, steady) or R2 (rear position lamp, variable intensity); S1 (stop lamp, steady) or S2 (stop lamp, variable intensity); AR (reversing lamp, letters A and R may be mingled).
requirements.test_case: Compare the marked symbols with the approved function classes.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. 148R01).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '148R' followed by the correct series digits.

requirements.text: In case the lamp cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the lamp shall bear a horizontal arrow showing in which position the lamp is to be mounted.
requirements.test_case: For a side-specific lamp, inspect the marking for a horizontal arrow.

requirements.text: In case a mounting-side arrow is required, the arrow shall be directed outwards from the vehicle for the rear position lamp and, in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps, for the reversing lamp.
requirements.test_case: Check on the vehicle-mounted orientation that the arrow points outboard.

requirements.text: In case the lamp may be used as part of an assembly of two independent lamps, the additional letter "D" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for 'D' to the right of the relevant function symbol.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is used as part of an interdependent lamp system, the additional letter "Y" shall be placed to the right side of the function symbol.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for 'Y' to the right of the relevant function symbol.

requirements.text: In case the reversing lamp has reduced light distribution, the lamp shall bear a vertical arrow starting from a horizontal segment and directed downwards.
requirements.test_case: For a reduced-distribution version, inspect the marking for the downward vertical arrow with horizontal segment.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the approval marking.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the production sample for the presence of the approval marking.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: The lamp shall bear a marking of the rated voltage(s) (6 V, 12 V or 24 V) or the range of voltage, since it has non-replaceable light sources (and, where fitted, an electronic light source control gear, a variable luminous intensity control or a secondary operating mode).
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage or voltage range marking.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each light source module shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect each module for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each light source module shall bear its specific identification code, comprising the starting letters "MD" followed by the approval mark without the circle, followed by additional symbols or characters in case several non-identical modules are used.
requirements.test_case: Inspect each module for the MD identification code in the correct format.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the approval mark in the module identification code and the approval mark on the lamp shall be from the same applicant.
requirements.test_case: Compare the module code approval mark with the lamp approval and the applicant records.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, each light source module shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect each module for the rated voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the MD code matching the module.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source module(s) are used, the lamp shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for the rated voltage marking.

requirements.text: In case an electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control is part of the lamp but not included in the lamp body, it shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the external control unit for its identification number and manufacturer name.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.
requirements.test_case: Review the drawing and the sample to confirm the mark is on a part permanently joined to the light-emitting lens.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the boot lid or a door is opened.
requirements.test_case: Check on the vehicle that the approval mark is visible when installed or with the boot lid opened.

requirements.text: In case the outer lens is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
requirements.test_case: For a detachable lens design, inspect both the lens and the housing for the approval marking.

requirements.text: In case the outer lens is used for several devices bearing different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
requirements.test_case: Inspect each device body to confirm it carries only the marking of its own functions.

requirements.text: The approval marking, the applicant's trade name or mark, the rated voltage marking and, where applicable, the module identification code and voltage marking (3.3.3.5(b)) and the external control gear marking shall be affixed on the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp to confirm all these markings are present on it.

requirements.text: In case replaceable light source modules are used, the markings of paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the light source module itself.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module component for its required markings.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used for the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps (including the R150 retro-reflector), the mark shall be visible after installation.
requirements.test_case: Check on the vehicle that the single approval mark is visible after installation.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, no light-transmitting part of the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Review the design to confirm the lens and retro-reflector cannot be removed without removing the marked part.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used, the size of its components shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations (e.g. R148, R150) under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the components of the single mark and compare them with the minimum sizes in R148 and R150.

requirements.text: Each lamp function submitted for approval (rear position lamp, stop lamp, reversing lamp) shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN R148.
requirements.test_case: Review the type-approval test report to confirm every applicable paragraph 4 and 5 requirement was verified with a pass result for each function.

requirements.text: The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of UN Regulation No. 48 (and the Annexes referenced there), in the series of amendments in force at the time of application, that are pertinent to each lamp and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Check the lamp against the applicable R48 §5/§6 provisions verifiable at device level (e.g. colour, geometric visibility, apparent surface) and record the results.

requirements.text: The lamp shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which it may be subjected in such use, its satisfactory operation remains assured and it retains the characteristics prescribed by UN R148.
requirements.test_case: Run a vibration test representative of vehicle use, then re-measure the photometric and colorimetric characteristics and check the lamp functions.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources, or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the circuit design for separate light sources per function, or confirm that the tell-tale restriction is declared.

requirements.text: In case a manufacturer logo is incorporated in the rear position lamp, the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface shall incorporate only one logo, and all requirements for the rear position lamp function shall still be fulfilled.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp for a single logo and repeat the photometric and colour tests of the rear position lamp with the logo present.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be used.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the logo and compare it with the vehicle manufacturer's statement.

requirements.text: In case a logo is incorporated, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm².
requirements.test_case: Measure the projected logo light emitting surface in the reference axis direction from CAD or by measurement and check it is ≤ 100 cm².

requirements.text: The stop lamp and the reversing lamp shall not incorporate a logo.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the apparent surfaces of the stop and reversing lamp functions for the absence of any logo.

requirements.text: In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of LEDs wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source for the failure provisions.
requirements.test_case: Review the LED wiring schematic to identify the light-source groups used for the failure analysis.

requirements.text: In case of failure of any one light source in the rear position lamp, the stop lamp or the reversing lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent standard light distribution table of Annex 3, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure per UN R48 shall be produced.
requirements.test_case: Disable each LED group in turn and measure the intensity at the Annex 3 grid points, or verify that the failure signal output is produced.

requirements.text: In case the minimum intensity option is used for single light source failure, the maximum intensities shall not be exceeded when all light sources are illuminated.
requirements.test_case: Measure the maximum intensity over the distribution with all LEDs lit and compare it with the paragraph 5 maxima.

requirements.text: In case of failure of the variable intensity control of a rear position lamp of category R2 emitting more than the maximum value of category R1, the steady luminous intensity requirements of category R1 shall be fulfilled automatically.
requirements.test_case: Simulate failure of the variable intensity control and measure that the intensities fall within the R1 limits.

requirements.text: The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light sources approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128 (with no restriction on use), and/or light source modules, and/or non-replaceable light sources.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp and its bill of materials to confirm that only permitted light source types are used.

requirements.text: The lamp shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.
requirements.test_case: Perform radiated and conducted emission tests (e.g. per R10 ESA methods) and check them against the limits.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be designed so that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to fit the module in all incorrect orientations and positions and confirm this is not possible.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall only be removable with the use of tool(s).
requirements.test_case: Attempt to remove the module by hand without tools and confirm this is not possible.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall be tamperproof.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the module design for tamper-evident or tamper-resistant construction.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall, regardless of the use of tools, not be interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source.
requirements.test_case: Check the mechanical interface against UN approved light source caps and confirm it is incompatible.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), the light source module shall, regardless of the use of tools, not be interchangeable with any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.
requirements.test_case: Try swapping the modules between function positions and confirm that mechanical keying prevents it.

requirements.text: In case of replaceable light source module(s), when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device shall be met.
requirements.test_case: Replace the module with another sample bearing the same identification code and repeat the photometric measurements.

requirements.text: Unless otherwise specified, the lamp shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements with a voltage of 13.5 V (12 V system) or 28 V (24 V system) supplied at the lamp, or as specified by the applicant where the lamp is controlled by an electronic light source control gear or variable intensity control.
requirements.test_case: Supply the lamp at 13.5 V (or the declared operating condition) during all photometric and colour measurements.

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each lamp function on the reference axis (HV) shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure the luminous intensity at HV with a goniophotometer for each function and compare it with the paragraph 5 minimum.

requirements.text: The intensity of light emitted by each lamp function shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Perform a goniophotometric scan over the visible field and confirm that no value exceeds the paragraph 5 maximum.

requirements.text: Outside the reference axis, the intensity of each lamp function shall be not less than the product of the paragraph 5 minimum and the percentage given in the pertinent Annex 3 light distribution figure for each direction, or not less than the intensity value specified in that figure.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity at all Annex 3 grid points and compare it with the minimum multiplied by the grid percentage.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Annex 2, the intensity of each lamp function shall be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity across the Annex 2 geometric visibility field and check it against the required minimum.

requirements.text: The provisions of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity shall be observed for each lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Evaluate the goniophotometric data for local variations against the Annex 3 provisions.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D' deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the maximum intensity requirement when all lamps together are lit.
requirements.test_case: Measure the maximum intensity with both lamps lit.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or stop lamp is an assembly of two independent lamps marked 'D', it shall comply with the minimum intensity requirement if either lamp has failed.
requirements.test_case: Measure the minimum intensities with each lamp of the assembly switched off in turn.

requirements.text: In case the lamp is part of an interdependent lamp system marked 'Y', the system shall meet the requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.
requirements.test_case: Perform the photometric and colour tests with all interdependent lamps of the system operating together.

requirements.text: In case the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on a fixed and partly on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements at all fixed positions of the movable component(s).
requirements.test_case: Measure photometry, colour and outboard visibility at each fixed position of the movable component.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity control (R2 and/or S2), the control shall not generate signals which cause luminous intensities outside the range specified in paragraph 5.
requirements.test_case: Drive the control through its full signal range and measure that the intensities remain within the paragraph 5 range.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity control, the control shall not generate signals causing luminous intensities exceeding the respective steady luminous intensity maximum specified in paragraph 5 under night-time conditions (systems depending only on day/night) or under standard conditions (other systems).
requirements.test_case: Set the control to night-time or standard conditions and measure that the intensities do not exceed the R1/S1 maxima.

requirements.text: If the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, the ratio between the luminous intensities measured with both turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp turned on alone shall be at least 5:1 in the field between ±5° V and ±10° H, with all light sources in operation where a function contains more than one light source.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensities with both functions on and with the rear position lamp alone over the ±5° V/±10° H field and compute the ratio.

requirements.text: Compliance of the luminous intensities shall be demonstrated by tests carried out according to Annex 8.
requirements.test_case: Perform the photometric tests per the Annex 8 procedure and record the results.

requirements.text: The colour of the light emitted by each lamp function (red for rear position and stop lamp, white for reversing lamp) shall comply with the colour requirements when measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for that function in Annex 3.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates at grid points inside the Annex 3 field with a spectroradiometer, with the LEDs present in the lamp.

requirements.text: Outside the field of the light distribution grid, no sharp variation of colour shall be observed for any lamp function.
requirements.test_case: Visually or spectrally inspect the emitted colour outside the grid field for abrupt colour changes.

requirements.text: The light emitted by the rear position lamp (R1 or R2) shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 4 on each of the two samples supplied.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples at the Table 4 / Figure A3-I points, compared against the Table 4 limits.

requirements.text: In case of a steady rear position lamp (R1), the luminous intensity shall be at least 4 cd minimum (par. 4.8.3.1(a)) and shall not exceed 17 cd as a single lamp or 8.5 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. Within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 the intensity shall be at least 0.05 cd.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of the R1 function at the Figure A3-I grid points and the Table A2-1 visibility angles.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity rear position lamp (R2), the luminous intensity shall be at least 4 cd minimum and shall not exceed 42 cd as a single lamp or 21 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. Within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 the intensity shall be at least 0.05 cd.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of the R2 function at minimum and maximum intensity settings at the Figure A3-I points and the Table A2-1 angles.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with the stop lamp, its luminous intensity shall not exceed 60 cd below a plane forming an angle of 5° downward from the horizontal plane.
requirements.test_case: Measure the rear position lamp intensity at all points below 5°D and check that it is at most 60 cd.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1, the rear position lamp shall emit a luminous intensity of at least 0.05 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at the boundary directions of the Table A2-1 geometric visibility angles.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light against the red chromaticity boundaries.

requirements.text: The light emitted by the stop lamp (S1 or S2) shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 7 on each of the two samples supplied.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples at the Figure A3-I points, compared against the Table 7 limits.

requirements.text: In case of a steady stop lamp (S1), the luminous intensity shall be at least 60 cd minimum and shall not exceed 260 cd as a single lamp or 130 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. Within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 the intensity shall be at least 0.3 cd.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of the S1 function at the Figure A3-I grid points and the Table A2-1 visibility angles.

requirements.text: In case of a variable intensity stop lamp (S2), the luminous intensity shall be at least 60 cd minimum and shall not exceed 730 cd as a single lamp or 365 cd for a lamp marked "D". The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-I. Within the angles of geometric visibility of Table A2-1 the intensity shall be at least 0.3 cd (day) and 0.07 cd (night).
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of the S2 function in day and night modes at the Figure A3-I points and the Table A2-1 angles.

requirements.text: Within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1, the stop lamp shall emit at least the minimum luminous intensity given in Table 7.
requirements.test_case: Measure intensity at the boundary directions of the Table A2-1 geometric visibility angles.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the emitted light against the red chromaticity boundaries.

requirements.text: The light emitted by the reversing lamp (AR) shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements of Table 10 on each of the two samples supplied.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement of both samples at the Figure A3-V points, compared against the Table 10 limits.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall have a luminous intensity of at least 80 cd minimum. Its maximum luminous intensity shall not exceed 300 cd in or above the H-plane, 600 cd below the H-plane down to 5°D, and 8000 cd below 5°D. The standard light distribution shall follow Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of the reversing lamp at the Figure A3-V grid points and checks of the maxima in each vertical zone.

requirements.text: In case the reversing lamp is intended to be installed exclusively in a pair of devices (reduced light distribution), it shall achieve a photometric value of at least 25 cd up to an angle of 30° inwards.
requirements.test_case: Measure the reversing lamp intensity at the inboard directions up to 30° and verify at least 25 cd.

requirements.text: The colour of light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
requirements.test_case: Colorimetric measurement of the reversing lamp light against the white chromaticity boundaries.

requirements.text: Lamps shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved under UN R148, with compliance with the requirements of paragraph 5 (specific technical requirements for rear position, stop and reversing lamps) verified in production.
requirements.test_case: Compare production samples against the approved type documentation and re-run the paragraph 5 photometric and colorimetric checks.

requirements.text: For production lamps, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the values prescribed in UN R148 for the rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions.
requirements.test_case: Photometric measurement of production samples at all prescribed points, checking that each value is within 20 per cent of the R148 limits.

requirements.text: For the minimum values required throughout the fields specified in Annexes 2 and 3, the measured values of production lamps shall correspond to Table 12. For a required minimum of 0.7 cd: 0.5 cd (20 per cent equivalent) and 0.3 cd (30 per cent equivalent). For 0.6 cd: 0.4 cd and 0.2 cd. For 0.3 cd: 0.2 cd and 0.1 cd. For 0.07 cd: 0.05 cd and 0.03 cd. For 0.05 cd: 0.03 cd and 0.02 cd.
requirements.test_case: Measure luminous intensity of production samples at the field-of-visibility minimum points and compare with the Table 12 equivalents.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1 or R2) shall provide minimum angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard horizontally and 15° above / 15° below vertically. The inboard horizontal angle may be reduced to 20° only below the H-plane for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm. The angle below may be reduced to 5° for lamps installed with the H-plane at a mounting height of less than 750 mm. Angles are given for a right-side lamp and are mirrored for a left-side lamp.
requirements.test_case: Goniometric check of the rear position lamp across the specified horizontal and vertical angular field, confirming light emission and the minimum intensity at the declared mounting height.

requirements.text: The minimum luminous intensities of the rear position lamp and the stop lamp in the various directions of measurement shall be the percentages given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits, with H = 0° and V = 0° being the reference axis passing through the centre of reference.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement at each grid point, compared with the axial minimum multiplied by the figure percentage and rounded down to three significant digits.

requirements.text: In case the rear position lamp or the S1/S2 stop lamp is intended to be installed with the manufacturer-specified H plane at a mounting height of 750 mm or less above the ground, the photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: Check the declared mounting height and limit the photometric verification to 5° down where it is 750 mm or less.

requirements.text: Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light intensity of the rear position lamp and the stop lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value, as a percentage, shown on the grid lines surrounding that direction.
requirements.test_case: Scan the intensity between grid points and verify that no value is below the lowest surrounding grid minimum.

requirements.text: If visual examination of the reversing lamp appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower of the two minimum intensities prescribed for those directions.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the reversing lamp beam and, if it is non-uniform, measure the intensities between adjacent measuring points against 50 % of the lower prescribed minimum.

requirements.text: The rear position lamp (R1/R2) and the stop lamp (S1/S2) shall achieve, in the various directions of measurement, at least the minimum intensities given in Figure A3-I as percentages of the minimum intensities required in Tables 4 and 7 respectively.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometric measurement at all Figure A3-I points for each function (and for each intensity level in case of R2/S2), compared with the percentage of the table minimum.

requirements.text: The reversing lamp shall achieve, in each measuring direction expressed in degrees from the axis of reference, at least the minimum intensities in cd given in Figure A3-V.
requirements.test_case: Goniophotometer measurement of the reversing lamp at all Figure A3-V points, compared with the cd minima.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp light distribution, the directions H = 0° and V = 0° shall correspond to the axis of reference, which on the vehicle is horizontal, parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, oriented in the required direction of visibility and passing through the centre of reference.
requirements.test_case: Verify the declared reference axis and centre of reference in the photometric test set-up and drawings.

requirements.text: Mass-produced lamps shall conform to the approved type from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimensions and geometry of production samples and compare them with the approved drawings and tolerances.

requirements.text: Any mass-produced lamp chosen at random shall meet the photometric performance requirements when tested according to paragraph 4.8 of this Regulation (rear position lamp, stop lamp and reversing lamp functions).
requirements.test_case: Take a random production lamp and measure the luminous intensity of each function at the Annex 3 points per paragraph 4.8, comparing the results with the limits.

requirements.text: The light emitted by mass-produced lamps shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates (red for the rear position and stop lamps, white for the reversing lamp) when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9 of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function on production samples per paragraph 4.9 and check them against the colour boundaries.

requirements.text: Mass-produced lamps shall not differ mechanically or geometrically from the approved type by more than inevitable manufacturing deviations.
requirements.test_case: Measure dimensions and inspect the construction of series lamps against the approved type drawings and record any deviations.

requirements.text: When a randomly chosen mass-produced lamp is tested for the photometric performances of paragraph 4.8, no measured value shall deviate from the values prescribed in paragraph 6.1.3.
requirements.test_case: Measure the luminous intensity of each function of a randomly selected production lamp at the prescribed points and compare it with the paragraph 6.1.3 limits.

requirements.text: Mass-produced lamps shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of each function of a production lamp under paragraph 4.9 conditions and check them against the colour boundaries.

requirements.text: For the reversing lamp (LED technology), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Switch on the reversing lamp from cold and measure the luminous intensity distribution after 1 minute (or derive it via the HV ratio); check it against the AR min/max values.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp and the stop lamp (LED technology), the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Measure each function's intensity distribution after 1 minute of operation (or derive it via the HV ratio) and check it against the R1/R2 and S1/S2 min/max values.

requirements.text: For the rear position lamp and the stop lamp (LED technology), the luminous intensities measured either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.
requirements.test_case: Operate each function for 30 minutes or until photometric stability, then perform a goniophotometer measurement against the min/max values.

requirements.text: Depending on the light source technology, the luminous intensity distribution of each lamp function shall, in addition to the requirements of paragraph 1, comply at the point in time after switch-on listed in Table A8-1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the intensity at the reference coordinate at the specified time after switch-on and scale the paragraph 1 distribution to confirm compliance.

requirements.text: Points in time after switch ON for additional testing: rear position lamp 4 s (reference coordinate HV); stop lamp 0.2 s (HV); reversing lamp 0.2 s (HV).
requirements.test_case: Use time-resolved photometry at HV to check intensity at 4 s (rear position) and 0.2 s (stop, reversing) after switch-on.

requirements.text: In case a lamp function uses LED technology only, the lamp function is deemed to comply with the intensity requirements at all points in time if the values measured according to paragraph 1.2 are compliant.
requirements.test_case: Confirm the functions are LED-only and that the 1 min / 10 min / 30 min (or stability) measurements comply.

requirements.text: In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the minimum intensity requirements of each lamp function shall be complied with at all points in time, starting at the point in time listed in Table A8-1 (rear position 4 s, stop 0.2 s, reversing 0.2 s) and ending when photometric stability is reached.
requirements.test_case: Record intensity at HV continuously from switch-on until stability and verify the minimum values are met from the Table A8-1 time onward.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for either the Unique Identifier and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or the approval marking and the other markings defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the drawing and sample to confirm a marking area large enough for the approval marking/UI and the TOP marking where required.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be clearly legible.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the markings on production samples for legibility.

requirements.text: All markings on the retro-reflector shall be indelible.
requirements.test_case: Perform a rub/durability check (e.g. solvent wipe) on the markings and confirm they remain intact.

requirements.text: The size of the approval marking shall be based on the value 'a' defined in Table 1.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimension 'a' of the approval mark on the sample.

requirements.text: For a retro-reflector for motor vehicles of Class IA (independent) or Class IB (combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight), the minimum value of 'a' for the approval marking is 5 mm.
requirements.test_case: Measure the approval mark and confirm 'a' ≥ 5 mm.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the approval mark: a circle surrounding the letter 'E' followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the circled 'E' and the country number.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number that is part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking and compare the sequential number with the approval certificate.

requirements.text: The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking layout to confirm the sequential number is adjacent to the circled E.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the symbol identifying the retro-reflective device prescribed in paragraph 3.2.5.: in case the lamp containing the retro-reflector is watertight (independent retro-reflector), the symbol 'IA'; in case the retro-reflector is combined with signal lamps that are not watertight, the symbol 'IB'.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for the class symbol IA or IB matching the approved class.

requirements.text: The approval marking shall include the number of this Regulation followed by the letter 'R' and the two digits indicating the series of amendments in force at the time of issue of the approval (e.g. '150R01').
requirements.test_case: Inspect the marking for '150R' followed by the correct series-of-amendments digits.

requirements.text: In case the approval marking is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format shown in Figure I of paragraph 3.3.3.1.
requirements.test_case: Compare the UI mark on the sample with the format of Figure I.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the sample for the applicant's trade name or mark.

requirements.text: The Class IA or IB retro-reflector shall bear the word 'TOP' inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.
requirements.test_case: Check whether the photometry depends on rotation; if so, inspect for a horizontal 'TOP' at the highest part of the illuminating surface.

requirements.text: The approval marking or the Unique Identifier, and the markings of paragraph 3.3.4., shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect the marking location on the sample for legibility.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark with the sequential number or Unique Identifier is used for the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated rear lamp approved under several UN Regulations, the marking shall be visible after installation of the lamp.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the lamp installed or in a vehicle-representative fixture to confirm the single mark is visible.

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used for the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, no part of the lamps that transmits light shall be removable without at the same time removing the approval mark with the sequential number or the Unique Identifier.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the design to confirm the mark sits on a part whose removal is required to remove any light-transmitting part (e.g. on the outer lens).

requirements.text: In case a single approval mark is used for the grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the size of the components of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
requirements.test_case: Measure the components of the single mark and compare them with the minimum sizes required by R150 (a ≥ 5 mm) and R148.

requirements.text: The requirements of sections 5 'General specifications' and 6 'Individual specifications' of UN Regulation No. 48 (and the annexes referenced there) pertinent to the red rear retro-reflector and to vehicle category M1 shall be applied, where their verification at the moment of retro-reflector type approval is feasible.
requirements.test_case: Review the R48 rear retro-reflector provisions (e.g. shape, colour, visibility angles) that can be verified on the device and check compliance by inspection and measurement.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall be so constructed that it functions satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Verify that the photometric and colorimetric requirements are met before and after the prescribed resistance tests (heat, water, corrosion, fuel, oil).

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to its efficient operation or to its maintenance in good condition.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect samples for moulding defects, sink marks, voids or damaged prisms, and review the design.

requirements.text: The components of the retro-reflector or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
requirements.test_case: Attempt to dismantle the retro-reflector by hand and with simple tools, and confirm it cannot be removed without destruction or special effort.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall be easy to clean.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the exposed outer surface and perform a cleaning trial.

requirements.text: The outer surface of the retro-reflector shall not be rough, and any protuberances on it shall not prevent easy cleaning.
requirements.test_case: Inspect and measure the surface roughness and the geometry of any protuberances on the outer surface.

requirements.text: There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflector when in normal use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the assembled lamp and confirm the prism (inner) surface cannot be reached without dismantling.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter (e.g. a colourless prism unit behind the red outer lens acting as filter), the optical unit and the filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
requirements.test_case: Inspect the attachment of the optical unit to the filter/lens and attempt separation under normal-use handling.

requirements.text: The retro-reflecting optical unit and any filter shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.
requirements.test_case: Inspect and analyse the material and confirm the colouring is in the bulk material, with no paint or varnish layer.

requirements.text: When the retro-reflector is illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, the angle specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1), the trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity shall be within the limits for red night-time retro-reflected colour defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the retro-reflected light under Illuminant A at 1/3° divergence and 0° illumination, and compare it with the R48 red limits.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
requirements.test_case: Visually inspect and measure the retro-reflector shape and dimensions against Annex 5, paragraph 1.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements of paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI and night-time chromaticity of the samples per Part 1 of Annex 4 and paragraph 4.2.1.

requirements.text: Every retro-reflector of Class IA or IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements of paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective device.
requirements.test_case: Run the resistance test sequence of Table 4 (heat, water, fuels, oils, corrosion, rear face, stability, weathering) and inspect the samples.

requirements.text: The retro-reflector shall meet the colorimetric requirements of paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI requirements of paragraph 5.1.4. when examined at least one hour after the heat resistance test of Part 1 of Annex 6. RI is checked at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.).
requirements.test_case: After 48 h at 65 °C and at least 1 h rest, measure colour and RI at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

requirements.text: After the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1. (water penetration, fuels and lubricants, corrosion where applicable, rear-face abrasion where applicable, stability in time, weathering), the retro-reflectors in each group shall have a colour that satisfies paragraph 5.1.5.
requirements.test_case: After each group's tests, visually inspect the colour and, in case of doubt, measure the trichromatic coordinates.

requirements.text: After the tests of paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have an RI that satisfies paragraph 5.1.4. This is verified at an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
requirements.test_case: After each group's tests, measure RI at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0° and compare with the Table 3 red values.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector has essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the retro-reflector shall have an RI satisfying paragraph 5.1.4. (at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°) and a colour satisfying paragraph 5.1.5. after the corrosion test of Part 4 of Annex 6.
requirements.test_case: Perform the salt-spray corrosion test (24 h, 2 h interval, 24 h), then inspect and measure RI and colour.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector is mirror-backed with an accessible rear face, the retro-reflector shall have an RI satisfying paragraph 5.1.4. (at 20', β1 = β2 = 0°) and a colour satisfying paragraph 5.1.5. after the rear-face abrasive-strength test of Part 5 of Annex 6.
requirements.test_case: Brush the rear face and apply the fuel mixture per Part 5 of Annex 6, then measure RI at 20' and β1 = β2 = 0°.

requirements.text: Where more than one axis of reference, or a range of axes, is specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the RI requirements with reference to each specified axis of reference or to the extreme axes of the specified range.
requirements.test_case: Repeat the photometric measurements for each declared reference axis and for the extremes of a declared range.

requirements.text: For photometric measurements of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system, as indicated by the manufacturer, and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered.
requirements.test_case: Check that the declared illuminating surface lies within a 200 mm diameter circle, and mask anything outside it during photometry.

requirements.text: The illuminating surface considered for photometric measurements of the Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall be limited to 100 cm²; the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not attain this area.
requirements.test_case: Measure the declared illuminating area and confirm it does not exceed 100 cm².

requirements.text: When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values of the red Class IA/IB retro-reflector shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in mcd/lx, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
requirements.test_case: Perform complete goniophotometric measurement of RI at all Table 3 angle combinations.
Compare the measured RI at each angle combination with these minimum values.

requirements.text: RI values of the retro-reflector lower than the minimum values for the outer illumination angles of Table 3 shall not occur within the solid angle that has the centre of reference as its apex and is bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).
requirements.test_case: Scan RI inside the bounded solid angle and confirm no value falls below the boundary minimum values.

requirements.text: In case the Class IA/IB retro-reflector is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height below 750 mm above the ground, the RI values shall be met only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
requirements.test_case: For a declared mounting height below 750 mm, verify the downward RI values only up to 5° below the H plane.

requirements.text: When tested according to paragraph 4.2.1. (night-time colour), the trichromatic coordinates of the luminous flux reflected by the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colour red specified in UN Regulation No. 48.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity of the retro-reflected light under the paragraph 4.2.1 illumination and check it against the R48 red boundaries.

requirements.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall conform to the approved type from a mechanical and geometric standpoint, with differences not exceeding inevitable manufacturing deviations within the requirements of this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimensions and geometry of production retro-reflectors and compare them with the approved drawings and the R150 shape and dimension limits.

requirements.text: When testing the photometric performance of any mass-produced retro-reflective device chosen at random, no measured value shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation.
requirements.test_case: Measure the CIL of randomly selected production retro-reflectors at the prescribed angles and check that every value is at least 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum.

requirements.text: Mass-produced retro-reflective devices shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates for red.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of production retro-reflector samples (including the red outer lens filter, if applicable) and verify they lie within the red boundaries.

requirements.text: For conformity of production, the mechanical and geometric differences of mass-produced retro-reflectors from the approved type shall not exceed inevitable manufacturing deviations.
requirements.test_case: Measure the dimensions and inspect the construction of randomly selected production retro-reflectors against the approved drawings and tolerances.

requirements.text: When the photometric performance of any mass-produced retro-reflector chosen at random is tested, no measured value (coefficient of luminous intensity) shall deviate unfavourably by more than 20 per cent from the minimum values prescribed in this Regulation; retro-reflectors with apparent defects are disregarded.
requirements.test_case: Measure the CIL of randomly selected production retro-reflectors at all prescribed angles and check that every value is at least 80 per cent of the prescribed minimum.

requirements.text: Mass-produced retro-reflectors shall comply with the prescribed chromaticity coordinates for red.
requirements.test_case: Measure the chromaticity coordinates of randomly selected production retro-reflectors and check that they fall within the red limits of R150.

requirements.text: In case of a Class IA (watertight) retro-reflector, mass-produced retro-reflectors shall pass the resistance-to-water-penetration test of paragraph 1 of Part 2 of Annex 6.
requirements.test_case: Subject a production retro-reflector to the Annex 6 Part 2 paragraph 1 water penetration test and verify that it meets the test's pass criteria.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", when rotated about its axis of reference at an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the angle specified in paragraph 5) and an angle of divergence of 20', the retro-reflector shall meet the CIL (RI) value specified in paragraph 5 even in the rotational position of minimum RI.
requirements.test_case: Rotate the sample about its reference axis on a goniophotometer at β=0°, α=20', find the minimum RI and compare it with the paragraph 5 value.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector is not marked "TOP", the retro-reflector shall meet the CIL values for the other illumination and divergence angles in the rotational position ε of minimum RI, or within ±5° of that position about the axis of reference.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at all prescribed β/α combinations with the sample set to the minimum-RI ε position, rotating it up to ±5° if needed, and compare the readings with paragraph 5.

requirements.text: In case the retro-reflector is marked "TOP", its RI shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed during rotation of ±5° about its axis of reference, at an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° (or the specified angle) and an angle of divergence of 20'.
requirements.test_case: Rotate the TOP-marked sample ±5° about its reference axis at β=0°, α=20' and verify that RI stays at or above the prescribed minimum throughout the rotation.

requirements.text: If the retro-reflector produces a mirror effect when its RI is measured at β1 = β2 = 0°, the RI requirement for that direction shall be met with the reading taken at β1 = -5°, β2 = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Turn the sample slightly about β=0° to check for a mirror effect; if one is present, measure RI at β1=-5°, β2=0° and compare it with the requirement.

requirements.text: If at β1 = β2 = 0° and ε = 0° the RI of the retro-reflector exceeds the specified value by 50 per cent or more, the retro-reflector shall meet the CIL values for all illumination and divergence angles at ε = 0°.
requirements.test_case: Measure RI at β=0°, ε=0°; if it is at least 150 % of the specified value, measure all prescribed angles at ε=0° and compare them with the limits.

requirements.text: The retro-reflection performance (CIL) of the retro-reflector shall be achieved when it is illuminated with CIE Standard Illuminant A (ISO 11664-2:2007(E)/CIE S 014-2/E:2006).
requirements.test_case: Perform the CIL measurements with a source calibrated to CIE Standard Illuminant A and verify that the paragraph 5 values are met.
